extracted.intended_audience: educational institutions (K–12 and postsecondary), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to Department of Education final Title IX regulations explaining standards for actual knowledge, reporting and investigative obligations, the scope of an 'education program or activity', and related procedural rules for K–12 and postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge — elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations expand the definition of actual knowledge to include notice to any employee of an elementary and secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For K–12 recipients, notice to any employee triggers the recipient's Title IX obligations; the Department incorporated this expansion to address commenters' concerns about trusted adults in elementary and secondary schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge — postsecondary limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: For postsecondary institutions, actual knowledge is not expanded beyond notice to the Title IX Coordinator and officials with authority to institute corrective measures on the recipient's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department disagrees with commenters seeking a wider pool of postsecondary employees; actual knowledge for colleges/universities remains focused on officials who can institute corrective measures (aligns with Gebser/Davis usage in private suits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge includes allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual knowledge means notice of sexual harassment or allegations of sexual harassment; the recipient need not have received facts definitively indicating denial of equal access for the obligation to respond to be triggered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to §106.30 definition and §106.44(a); partial information or allegations are sufficient to require a prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response and outreach to the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response and supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient has actual knowledge, it must respond promptly and non-deliberately indifferently, including offering supportive measures to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 106.44(a) requires the Title IX Coordinator to promptly contact the complainant to discuss supportive measures (as defined in §106.30), consider complainant's wishes, inform them of availability with or without filing a formal complaint, and explain the formal complaint process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, accessible reporting options and notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must have clear, accessible reporting options and must notify their educational community about how to report sexual harassment in person, by mail, telephone, or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These final regulations go beyond the Gebser/Davis framework by requiring recipients to maintain and publicize accessible reporting channels; any person may report (complainant need not be the reporter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may initiate an investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the complainant or the Title IX Coordinator may initiate an investigation that starts the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party reports trigger outreach and supportive measures but do not by themselves initiate an investigation; the Title IX Coordinator may, however, initiate an investigation despite a complainant's request for confidentiality if not investigating would be 'clearly unreasonable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant autonomy and two-track reporting model
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants may choose to report for the purpose of receiving supportive measures without initiating an investigation, and can later file a formal complaint to start an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes similarities to the military 'restricted/unrestricted' model: respect victim autonomy to receive services only or to pursue investigation; Title IX Coordinator must balance complainant wishes with safety/obligation to investigate in extraordinary cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education program or activity — substantial control standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §§106.30, 106.44, and 106.45, 'education program or activity' includes 'locations, events, or circumstances over which the recipient exercised substantial control over both the respondent and the context in which the harassment occurs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department adds this language (mirroring Davis) to clarify jurisdictional scope; whether off-campus conduct falls within the program/activity depends on substantial control and other statutory/regulatory definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education program or activity — recognized student organization buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'education program or activity' also includes 'any building owned or controlled by a student organization that is officially recognized by a postsecondary institution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a bright-line rule: if an institution officially recognizes a student organization, buildings owned/controlled by that organization fall within Title IX obligations and the institution must offer supportive measures and may need to investigate formal complaints arising there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three conditions for off-campus coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's Title IX obligations extend to off-campus incidents if any of three conditions are met: (1) the incident occurs as part of the recipient's 'operations' pursuant to statutory/regulatory definitions; (2) the recipient exercised substantial control over the respondent and the context; or (3) the incident occurred in a building owned or controlled by an officially recognized student organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that 'off campus' does not automatically exclude Title IX coverage; institutions must analyze facts under these tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized student organizations — institutional leverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions may require, as part of official recognition, that student organizations that own or control buildings agree to abide by the recipient's Title IX policy and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although institutions may have limited control over off-campus private property, recognition creates an obligation to address harassment in such buildings and allows investigation (e.g., interviewing students) even if gathering evidence is more difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant/respondent identity and filing limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The definitions of 'complainant' and 'respondent' are not limited by affiliation with the recipient (any person may be a complainant or respondent), but to file a formal complaint the complainant must be 'participating in or attempting to participate in' the recipient's education program or activity at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the ability to reach persons outside the recipient's community for outreach/supportive measures while limiting formal investigative obligations to those related to the recipient's programs/activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to dismiss when respondent no longer affiliated
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may, in its discretion, dismiss a formal complaint if the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed by the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes that where the recipient lacks disciplinary authority over the respondent, completing a grievance process may not be required (§106.45(b)(3)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-factor consideration for program/activity scope — no single determinative factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts and recipients may consider multiple factors (e.g., recipient ownership of premises, endorsement, oversight, supervision, disciplinary power, funding/promotion/sponsorship) to determine whether conduct occurred in a program or activity, but no single factor is determinative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should evaluate the totality of circumstances to determine whether they exercised 'substantial control' over respondent and context; the Department notes that court-applied factors may be helpful but are not dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party reports require the recipient to reach out to the complainant and offer supportive measures but do not permit the third party to initiate an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations preserve third-party reporting to lower barriers to access services while protecting complainant control over initiating grievance processes; complainants may later file formal complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department's regulatory authority bounded by Title IX statutory scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's authority to regulate sexual harassment derives from Title IX and is co-extensive with the statute's scope regarding 'education program or activity'; Title IX does not authorize regulation of sex discrimination occurring everywhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department interprets statutory text and existing regulatory definitions (20 U.S.C. 1687; 34 CFR 106.2(h)) and aligns regulatory language with Supreme Court's application in Davis to ensure authority is properly exercised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from Clery Act geography
rubrics_metrics.description: The revision referencing buildings owned or controlled by an officially recognized student organization is not the same as the Clery Act's use of 'noncampus building or property.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clery Act definitions/geography and Title IX scope serve distinct purposes; recipients should not conflate the two when assessing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee training/education concerns and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged that resident assistants, professors, coaches, and supervisors be educated about responding appropriately to disclosures and informing students about rights and reporting options; Department response clarifies who counts for actual knowledge and requires notification of reporting options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Department expanded actual-knowledge coverage for K–12 employees to include any employee, it did not expand the postsecondary reporting pool; nonetheless recipients must notify their educational communities of reporting options and ensure accessible reporting mechanisms.
